author: Inside Edition
description: At Lindsay Clancy's murder trial, the judge braced jurors for an excursion to the house where Clancy strangled her three children. Clancy sat stoned-faced and chose to not join the jurors for the tour. A police motorcade led jurors who boarded a chartered bus to the home in Duxbury, Massachusetts. The defense claims Clancy is not guilty of murder because she was suffering postpartum depression and postpartum psychosis.
title: Jurors Tour Home Where Lindsay Clancy Strangled Her Three Children

author: Inside Edition
description: A jet skier enjoying a day on the lake suffered a life-threatening crisis. He became unconscious and slumped over the jet ski while heading straight for the dock on popular Lake Lainer in Georgia. His friend recorded the incident. The jet ski crashed into the dock and he was thrown into the water. By some miracle, he is alive. Dillan Stapler, 32, told Inside Edition he has no memory of what happened. His friend Anthony Zilke saved him.
title: Jet Skier Survives Life-Threatening Crisis

author: Inside Edition
description: Oscar-winning animator Glen Keane, 72, was rescued by helicopter atop a jagged mountain ledge. Keane animated "Dear Basketball" and Disney classics like "The Little Mermaid" and "Beauty and the Beast." He found himself in trouble on Mummy Mountain outside Phoenix, Arizona, which he had climbed as a youngster. Keane's legs gave out and he knew he needed help to get back down. He drew an image of himself on the mountain as a kid just for Inside Edition.
title: 72-Year-Old Oscar-Winning Animator Rescued From Mountain

author: Inside Edition
description: A traffic court judge judged his own case. He was charged with the use of a handheld device  while driving. Judge Michel E. Henson tells Inside Edition's Steven Fabian it was the "absolute first time and hopefully the only time" he called himself to the bench. He ruled himself guilty and fined himself $60, the maximum penalty.
title: Judge Finds Himself Guilty Of Texting While Driving

author: Inside Edition
description: It's a little early for the spooky season, but the spiders in one part of the world have already decorated. The Sorek Creek in the mountains of Jerusalem looks somewhat enchanted after spiders have woven thick webs throughout trees and other vegetation. The creek reportedly contains treated sewage, which provides ample nutrients for a large mosquito population. Those mosquitos are prey for long jawed spiders known as Tetragnatha. Inside Edition Digital’s Mara Montalbano has more.
title: Thick, Massive Spiderwebs Take Over Trees

author: Inside Edition
description: In March, Amy McGorry asked the public to help her find a living donor who would be willing to give her a piece of their liver. Just three months later, she got the news that someone stepped up to help save her life. As shocked as she was at the good news, she was even more surprised to learn that she knew her donor personally, a woman by the name of Sue Filshie. Inside Edition Digital’s Mara Montalbano has more.
title: Woman Surprised To Learn Liver Transplant Donor Is Longtime Friend

author: Inside Edition
description: The popular tourist attraction on the Italian island of Capri is only accessible at low tide by rowboat.
title: Couple's Blue Grotto Visit Nearly Ends In Watery Disaster #shorts
